items.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I had that one opportunity, when we made that film, I had that boy that was there—Tony.

ctx.x: Is this a concept that you share with the people you perform with? Either the people in your band or when you’re a side person with other folks. Is this an approach that you discuss or share with other musicians?

Well nobody, they don’t—drummers are reluctant to come and ask things like that. I had that one opportunity, when we made that film, I had that boy that was there—Tony. And that different drummer! No, no I am talking about the kid! First he wanted me to

give him a drum set, but he went to a private school. And I said, “What’s the matter don’t they have a music department in your school?” He said, “No.” and I said, “Why don’t you get one!” And so he bugged the principals and he got a musical department in place in his school. He did that himself! (Laughs)
